=== CANAL : #tips-and-hints ===
==========================================
[2024-06-10 11:43] nicmo7829 : AVQ is not checked in the match engine, there is no team 1 AVQ vs Team 2 AVQ. The relevant skills of the players are compared in each play (by type of play). AVQ is just to visually simplify the quality of a player.
[2024-06-10 11:51] nicmo7829 : Even if you select the right Marking option against an opponent, keep in mind that Marking will only help in key passes from that category, not the others.  Example: You select Drop Deep Marking, the opponent selects Pass into Space approach (that leads to one on ones (OO) attacker vs goalkeeper). Your marking will counter ONLY the pass into space plays (Yellow in the ingame graphics), this means that whenever the opponent makes an attempt of an one on one, your defense plays with "extra power". All other play types you will suffer more, but they should be much less as your opponent is likely to play more into space than the other alternatives. This is true of all 3 types of plays.  If you check the stats of a match, you will likely find that all 3 types of play were made, if a manager selected a specific approach, then there will be more of that type.
[2024-06-10 11:57] nicmo7829 : -----
[2024-06-10 11:58] nicmo7829 : Every match, in each minute, there is a chance of a new play, Playing attacking will increase this chance while defending reduces it. If both teams are attacking, there will be plenty of plays and players will lose more condition. Playing attacking is advised if you think you are better than the opponent, will generate more plays -> more scoring chances, if your better you should score more.
[2024-06-10 11:58] nicmo7829 : -----
[2024-06-10 12:04] nicmo7829 : in every play there is a "clash" between the attacker and defender where both players have their current skills modified by several aspects of the match and then the best one usually wins. there are plenty of factors that modify their skills; his team playing home/away, is he defending and does he have a yellow card, team morale, his team captain better than the opponent, player condition, did he take an energy bar at half time, traits, marking option, wrong position in the field, sent off team mates, formation of both teams. not in this particular order of importance.
[2024-06-18 12:22] nicmo7829 : ---- people often ask where to train players, if a striker uses this skill or another. i would like to point out this interesting information. If you check this match stats, or any other match, you can see almost all players try to tackle the opponent at some point in the match, even strikers. What helps this tackle to succeed or not is the player defensive skills vs the attacker attacking skills. So if your midfielders and strikers have high tackling, you will have a much higher chance of ending that build up attempt right from the start and winning the ball. Midfielders often tackle a lot, so make sure you get midfielders with high tackling too if possible 🙂
[2024-07-04 10:19] nicmo7829 : The game is about increasing the odds of winning. With player skills, condition, tactics, external factors (morale, home/away, etc), red cards, yellow cards, injuries, etc. With these factors, actions and decisions you can increase the odds. Obviously you are playing other managers that try in their own way to achieve the same thing.  The best team wont always win, same as in real life, all you can do is increase your chances, same as in real life
[2024-07-12 09:07] nicmo7829 : the match engine is not scripted in any way, each build up is simulated and has 4 stages, each 4 stage players get 1on1 checked on their skills(after getting modified), the best player has a higher chance of winning the duel. Thats 4 duels per build up, in a game there is 60-80 duels, the best team can lose by 0-10, however highy unlikely
[2024-07-12 09:09] nicmo7829 : Nowhere does AVQ get checked in the match engine, a match of 50AVQ vs 53AVQ is a very similar match in terms of AVQ, the outcome will most likely be better for the team with skills in the best places.
[2024-07-12 09:11] nicmo7829 : If you have fast attacking players, better play "pass into space", these skills will be checked often in these situations, if you have strong players in the attack, cross to box. The same for your opponent, if he has slow defenders in the wings, play pass into space using the sides. If the DCs are slow, go middle. MAXIMISE your chances with what you have. You can still lose but gets easier and easier to win if you MAXIMISE. You can also get all these decisions wrong and win, however it is unlikely.
[2024-07-12 09:51] nicmo7829 : KOB simulates 10.000 matches per day, you can find all sort of results and crazy stuff, like in real life really
[2024-08-23 19:20] nicmo7829 : <@705349843798982707> 's excel sheet to predict/test skills and check how they affect the average quality of a player

[2024-07-24 16:04] nicmo7829 : guys, i need your help explaining how formations work in KOB in the documentation, so if you can tell me if this is understandable or not and if you have more questions about it, maybe i can add more information.  **************************  Formations  There are several formations to choose from, 4-4-2 being the default and most neutral formation. Any other formation may bring bonuses or penalties to a determined play. For example, a defending team using 5-3-2 will see a benefit when one of the 5 defenders is going for a tackle. However if the same team is defending using 3-4-3, the same defender will be less effective as they are missing 1 player. The same is true if the player defending is a midfielder or striker, the match engine will also check how many players there are in that position. Same logic when attacking, a lone striker in a 4-5-1 will struggle to score, comparing to 3-4-3 but since his midfield has 5 players, he will probably be served more often.  So, we can assume that in KOB, 5-3-2 is a defensive formation, 3-4-3 is an attacking formation that will be weaker defending but every attack using a striker is stronger.

[2024-08-06 15:46] nicmo7829 : It simple really... the match engine gives you X amount of plays for you and for your opponent in a single match, this amount depending on team mentality. In those X amount of plays you need to maximize them in order to get the best comparisons between attacking player skills vs defending player skills, you can do this with your tactical decisions that can raise or lower your player skills for that given comparison. The outcome can vary, the bigger the skill stack on your side, the better the chances of your player winning that comparison (buildup, keypass, shot creation, shot).

(200 because thats the attackers skills)

[2024-09-19 23:06] waggy13 : For everyone struggling with how they “think” the game works:  Stop thinking of it as a football game.  This is still a game run by a computer so every stop has to go in specific order to generate an outcome.  Think of each step more of as a dice game.  Player gets ball- Roll dice for if he keeps it, this is effected by speed, positioning, and technique(i don’t have the answers on the exact skills involved).  then player moves to next step.  The higher the skills the bigger/higher the dice can go, but low/bad outcome can still happen because again all dice start at 1.  Then there are things that can affect the dice also like determination.  I can get more specific if anyone wants me to but this is how i see the game and how i make decisions on my players and why a balanced player is better than putting all points on charisma, this is also how i deal with losing games 🤣.
